name: Adobe Photoshop
description: Adobe Photoshop is the industry-standard raster image editor, used for photo retouching, compositing, digital painting, graphic design, matte painting, web and UI mockups, and print production. It is built around a layered document model: pixel layers, adjustment layers, smart objects, shape and type layers, layer styles, masks (pixel, vector and clipping) and blend modes, all stacked inside a document with one or more artboards. Around that model sit a toolbar of roughly sixty tools, a menu system covering selection, image, layer, type, filter and view operations, dozens of dockable panels, and a growing set of Adobe Firefly generative AI features (Generative Fill, Generative Expand, Generate Image, Generate Background, Remove tool). Photoshop reads and writes its own layered .psd/.psb formats plus every common raster and camera raw format, and integrates with Camera Raw, Adobe Bridge, Creative Cloud Libraries and the Photoshop cloud API.

automation.summary: Photoshop is automated in five main ways. (1) ExtendScript (JSX): the classic ES3-based JavaScript DOM (`app`, `app.activeDocument`, `ArtLayer`, `Selection`, `PathItem`, `TextItem`), run from File > Scripts > Browse..., from the Scripts menu when the .jsx file is placed in Presets/Scripts, by double-clicking a .jsx whose first line is `#target photoshop`, or by passing the script path to the executable (`Photoshop.exe "C:\path\script.jsx"`). (2) Action Manager / batchPlay descriptors, which reach every command the DOM does not expose, via `executeAction`/`executeActionGet` with `stringIDToTypeID`. (3) UXP: the modern plugin and scripting runtime (`require('photoshop').app`, `action.batchPlay`, `core.executeAsModal`), with .psjs script files and UXP plugins built in the UXP Developer Tool. (4) COM automation on Windows through the `Photoshop.Application` ProgID, whose `Open`, `DoJavaScript`, `DoJavaScriptFile`, `DoAction` and `ActiveDocument` members let Python (pywin32), C#, VBScript or PowerShell drive a running Photoshop. (5) No-code automation: recorded Actions (.atn) played through File > Automate > Batch, droplets, and the Image Processor. Separately, the cloud-hosted Photoshop API (part of Adobe Firefly Services) performs PSD edits server-side over REST with no desktop install.

cli.description: Launch Photoshop (or hand the file to an already-running instance) and execute an ExtendScript file. The script should start with `#target photoshop` so the file type is routed to Photoshop. Photoshop may show the "You should only run scripts from a trusted source" alert the first time; launching via `start "" photoshop.exe script.jsx` or from the Scripts menu avoids it.
Fire-and-forget launch from a .bat file or CI job. Photoshop is a GUI application with no true headless mode, so an interactive desktop session must be available.
Open a document from the command line. Combine with a Script Events Manager event (File > Scripts > Script Events Manager, event "Open Document") to run a script automatically on every opened file.
Drive Photoshop from an external process on Windows through COM without writing a .jsx launcher. `DoJavaScript(code)` runs a string of ExtendScript instead of a file.

apis.name: ExtendScript (JSX) DOM
apis.description: The long-standing scripting interface. `app` is the Application object; `app.documents`, `app.activeDocument`, `Document.artLayers`, `layerSets`, `channels`, `pathItems`, `selection` and `TextItem` form the object tree. Units follow `app.preferences.rulerUnits`, so set it explicitly; suppress modal dialogs with `app.displayDialogs = DialogModes.NO`. Scripts are ES3 JavaScript with Adobe's File/Folder objects and the ScriptUI dialog toolkit.

apis.name: Action Manager (executeAction)
apis.description: Low-level descriptor API that plays the same internal commands the UI uses, covering everything the DOM omits. Build an `ActionDescriptor`, address targets with `ActionReference`, convert names to integer type IDs with `stringIDToTypeID` (or the legacy `charIDToTypeID`), then call `executeAction`. `executeActionGet` reads document, layer and application properties back. The ScriptingListener plugin records the descriptors for any UI action.

apis.name: UXP scripting and plugins
apis.description: The modern runtime (Photoshop 22+ for plugins, 23.3+ for .psjs scripts). `require('photoshop').app` exposes a promise-based DOM; `action.batchPlay(descriptors, options)` plays actionJSON descriptors; anything that changes the document must run inside `core.executeAsModal(fn, {commandName})`. File access goes through `require('uxp').storage.localFileSystem`. UXP plugins add panels built with HTML/CSS/JS and are debugged with the UXP Developer Tool.

apis.name: COM automation (Windows)
apis.description: Photoshop registers the `Photoshop.Application` ProgID (version-specific ProgIDs such as `Photoshop.Application.180` also exist). Any COM client can create it, open documents, play recorded Actions with `DoAction(actionName, actionSetName)` and evaluate ExtendScript with `DoJavaScript(code)` or `DoJavaScriptFile(path, args, execMode)`. The return value of `DoJavaScript` is the value of the last expression, which is the usual way to get data back out.
apis.example:
import win32com.client as win32
ps = win32.Dispatch("Photoshop.Application")
ps.Visible = True
ps.Open(r"C:\in\shot.psd")
ps.DoAction("Web export", "My Actions")
n = ps.DoJavaScript("app.activeDocument.layers.length")
ps.ActiveDocument.Close(2)  # 2 = do not save changes

apis.name: Actions, Batch and Droplets
apis.description: The no-code automation layer. Record a sequence in the Actions panel, save the set as an .atn file, then replay it over a folder with File > Automate > Batch, or export it as a droplet executable that processes any files dropped onto it. Actions can call scripts (Insert Menu Item > File > Scripts), so the two layers compose.
apis.example:
1. Actions panel > New Set "Web" > New Action "Export 1200px", press Record.
2. Run Image > Image Size (1200 px wide) and File > Save As (JPEG), then press Stop.
3. File > Automate > Batch: Set = Web, Action = Export 1200px, Source = Folder, Destination = Folder, tick "Override Action Save As Commands".

apis.name: Photoshop API (cloud REST)
apis.description: Server-side PSD manipulation in Adobe Firefly Services, with no Photoshop installation. Requests are JSON: inputs and outputs are presigned storage URLs (S3, Azure, Dropbox or Adobe's own), the call returns a job URL that is polled for status. v1 exposes `/pie/psdService/documentCreate`, `/documentOperations`, `/renditionCreate`, `/smartObject` and `/text`; v2 unifies them behind `/v2/create-composite`. Authentication is an Adobe IMS OAuth server-to-server token plus the `x-api-key` header.

apis.name: Photoshop plugins (UXP, CEP, C++ SDK)
apis.description: Three plugin surfaces coexist. UXP is the current one for panels and automation; CEP (HTML/CSS/JS extensions with a Node.js host) is legacy but still loads in current versions; the C++ Photoshop SDK builds file-format, filter, automation and selection plugins as native .8bi/.8be/.8ba modules. Plugins are distributed through Adobe Exchange and the Creative Cloud Desktop marketplace.
apis.example:
1. Install the UXP Developer Tool from Creative Cloud Desktop.
2. Create a plugin from the "Photoshop panel" template; edit manifest.json (entrypoints, requiredPermissions).
3. Click Load in UDT to side-load it into Photoshop, then Watch for hot reload while you edit.

file_formats.description: Photoshop Document: the native layered format holding layers, groups, masks, layer styles, smart objects, text, paths, channels, colour profile and metadata. Limited to 30,000 px per side and 2 GB.
Large Document Format. Same feature set as .psd but supports documents up to 300,000 px per side and files larger than 2 GB. Enable "Maximize Compatibility" or 32-bit work to see it offered.
Brush preset file: brush tips, dynamics, texture and dual-brush settings. Loaded from the Brushes panel menu > Import Brushes.
Actions set file. Holds one or more recorded actions; loaded from the Actions panel menu > Load Actions and required by Batch and droplets.
Layer Styles file containing one or more style presets (drop shadow, bevel, overlays). Loaded from the Styles panel menu.
Gradient preset file used by the Gradient tool, Gradient Map adjustment and Gradient Overlay layer effect.
Pattern preset file used by the Pattern Stamp tool, Fill > Pattern, Pattern Overlay and pattern fill layers.
Curves preset. Saved from the Curves dialog/adjustment and reloadable there; .acs, .ahu, .ale and similar hold other adjustment presets.
Colour swatches file loaded and saved from the Swatches panel.
ExtendScript file. Run from File > Scripts > Browse..., from the Scripts menu when placed in Presets/Scripts, or by passing the path to Photoshop.exe. `.jsxbin` is the compiled, obfuscated form.
UXP script file (Photoshop 23.3 and later). Modern JavaScript with `require('photoshop')`; run from File > Scripts and debuggable in the UXP Developer Tool.
Droplet: a small executable produced by File > Automate > Create Droplet that runs a chosen action over any files or folders dropped onto it.
Creative Cloud plugin package (UXP or CEP) installed through Creative Cloud Desktop or Adobe Exchange.
TIFF, which Photoshop can write with layers, transparency and a colour profile; the usual lossless interchange format for print.
Adobe Digital Negative and vendor raw files (.cr3, .nef, .arw, .raf). Opened through the Camera Raw plug-in, which can also be applied to any layer as Filter > Camera Raw Filter.
